reader.requirement: At --std 85 the end program header must be accepted exactly as END PROGRAM program-name followed by a separator period, with program-name a user-defined word (X.2.5.3 SR1, including words reserved only by later editions), closing a single or a contained program; forms outside the format (no period, no name, a literal name, END without PROGRAM, END FUNCTION closing a PROGRAM-ID, a duplicated header) must be refused. The witnesses cover only the END FUNCTION / FUNCTION-ID side.

edition-consulted.switches: a word reserved only in a later edition (TYPEDEF, FACTORY, VALIDATE) is a user-defined program-name at 85 and refused (COBOL0901) at 2023
refuses FUNCTION-ID (and so the END FUNCTION form) below 2002
from 2002 a containing program must have a procedure division before its contained programs; not the end header's format, same END PROGRAM keyword check at every edition

reader.edition-search: grep EditionContext/Edition.Year/DialectLevel in SourceUnitShape.cs and EndMarkerPass.cs (EndMarkerPass uses the edition only for the diagnostic cursor); VersionConformancePass searched for EndProgramHeader (no arm)
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no for the header itself: the same grammar rule and screens run at 85 and 2023; only the set of words admissible as program-name differs (later-reserved words are user words at 85), which the 85 arm gets right
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witnesses exercise END FUNCTION / FUNCTION-ID refusal at 85; none exercises END PROGRAM's own spellings, the period, or the program-name word class

single program with END PROGRAM SOLOP.: accepted
missing separator period after program-name: refused
END PROGRAM with no program-name: refused

reader.notes: endProgramHeader (END (PROGRAM|FUNCTION) programName DOT) is one rule for every edition; SourceUnitShape refuses END FUNCTION on a PROGRAM-ID and VersionConformancePass refuses FUNCTION-ID below 2002, so at 85 only END PROGRAM program-name. reaches a program. Diagnostics at 85 cite ISO 2023 clause numbers (COBOL2274, COBOL2793), a citation-presentation matter only.
reader.at-2023: p2a runs (OUTER/INNER), p2b refused identically; later-reserved program-names refused with COBOL0901

refuter.evidence: Probed the SRs the reader skipped, at --std 85: e1 END PROGRAM WRONGP closing SOLOP -> COBOL2793 name not identical (SR2); e2 nested end headers swapped -> COBOL2793 out of order (SR3); e8 inner program's end header missing -> COBOL2793 (GR1); e7 a DISPLAY after a separate program's END PROGRAM -> COBOL0001 (GR4); e6 two separately compiled programs each closed by END PROGRAM -> 'P1 / P2' (GR4 legal form); e9 lowercase 'end program solop.' -> runs (lowercase equivalent, §1985:IV.4.2.2.1); e11 extra spaces -> runs; e5 'SOLOP-' -> COBOL2773 hyphen last; e4 all-digit 12345 -> COBOL5506 (user word needs a letter, §1985:IV.4.2.2.1.1). Class c: e3 a 31-character name (legal at 2023, 63 max) -> COBOL1567 30-character maximum for COBOL-85; e3b 30 characters runs; e10 SOLO_P -> COBOL0900 underscore requires COBOL-2002 (runs at 2023); e12 PROGRAM-ID ...
